people.title: Kael
people.body: The hunter following Greyfen's road. His own promises cannot stand in for another person's agreement.

facts.body: Kael has admitted abandoning an escort and not returning. Giving that account does not erase what he did; what he chooses to do now remains his responsibility.

promises.body: Promise: remain while the people carrying the account need protection. Kael did not promise that nobody could be hurt.
Promise: stay and preserve a record that cannot simply be closed again.
Promise: remain with the road's living consequences. Kael chose his own part without pledging the households around him.
After the covenant, Kael took a place at the workbench. The next day's labor is now part of his promise.

people.title: Sister Anwen
people.body: Greyfen's shrine keeper. The people who come to her need care as well as an account of the road.

facts.body: The red-thread feathers connect Anwen's containment rite to Sella's journey. They establish a connection, not permission to give Anwen's future testimony.
Anwen's account continues at the cemetery gate. The disturbed graves offer further evidence to inspect.
The grain list is no longer a pledge sheet. Care and food remain separate from any invitation to speak.

people.title: Rook
people.body: A traveler and trader who knows Greyfen's road and the people who use it.

facts.body: Kael carried the flour clear of Rook's cart. The kitchen received it and the cart could be moved.

people.title: Mira Fen
people.body: Greyfen's herbalist. People come to her when practical care cannot wait.

facts.body: Kael inspected the garden. An inspected ingredient is evidence about the treatment, not a decision about what the families must accept.

people.title: Blacksmith Tor
people.body: The village blacksmith. A working hinge or a sound road matters to households as much as a weapon does.

facts.body: Kael cleared the drain and seated the boards while Tor drove the last peg. The kitchen cart can use the repaired road.

people.title: Widow Elna
people.body: Elna remembers Harl as someone she loved. Her grief is hers to share, and kindness remembered does not settle the questions about his actions.

people.title: Farmer Toma
people.body: A Greyfen farmer and a father. His family's safety and his neighbors' safety are connected.

people.title: Captain Senn
people.body: The captain whose men hold the bandit road. Kael has heard his voice in the account.
people.unavailable_body: Senn is no longer present to offer a living oath. The retained account remains evidence, not a promise made on his behalf.

facts.body: Senn's soldiers lowered their weapons and surrendered the road. That act did not absolve their conduct or make anybody a consenting witness.

people.title: Sir Halvern
people.unidentified_body: Kael has heard the armored witness's voice. This record has not yet established the witness's name.
people.body: The witness beneath Vargan, returning to the same road and the same order.

facts.body: Halvern's memory is bounded by what he experienced. It cannot supply knowledge of events that followed his death.

promises.body: Recorded choice: Halvern's bounded account has been kept. A dead witness's memory is not the consent of a living household.
Recorded choice: Halvern was released. The recovered command proof remains available without requiring his continued captivity.
Recorded choice: Halvern's binding was destroyed. The recovered human proof survives; no new promise can be taken from him.

people.title: Lord Edric Vargan
people.body: Vargan's lord. His decisions shape the road, the court and the village's supplies.

facts.body: Edric's renewal notice made support conditional on assent. Hunger does not turn those terms into a freely given promise.

people.title: Record Keeper Vale
people.body: The keeper of Vargan's records, encountered through the archive's account.

facts.body: The command proof has been recovered. It can establish the order without borrowing consent from the person who kept it.

people.title: Steward Merrow
people.body: Vargan's steward, arranging sacks and petitions in the court's daily business.

people.title: The White Hart
people.body: The presence at the end of the reopened road, asking Kael to answer for what he carries.

promises.body: The chosen resolution has been carried out. Its result does not erase the human records or the living people's responsibilities.

people.title: Bram Kett
people.body: One of the missing travelers. His belongings have given Kael a trace of the person behind the contract's name.

facts.body: The marked tool and repairs place Bram with the cart. He did not simply abandon it.

people.title: Sella Vey
people.body: One of the missing travelers, accompanied by her son Oren. Her account must be recovered from what survives of the journey.

facts.body: The red-thread feathers link her journey to the shrine's attempted containment.

people.title: Oren Vey
people.body: Sella's son, missing from the road with her and Bram. A recovered object is a trace of his life, not permission to expose every part of it.
